title: Human ECoG speaking consonant-vowel syllables
description: High-density (256-channel) electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded at the University of California, San Francisco from epilepsy patients who read aloud consonant-vowel syllables. The dataset includes 31 recording blocks from four subject codes, with hand-marked annotations of syllable onset, consonant-vowel transition and offset, rest baselines, and anatomical electrode labels. It supports research on the functional organization of human ventral sensorimotor cortex during speech articulation. Data are organized as iEEG-BIDS with the source NWB files preserved byte-identically.
methods_description: Cortical local field potentials were recorded with subdural high-density 256-channel ECoG arrays and a multichannel amplifier optically connected to a Tucker-Davis Technologies digital signal processor, sampled at about 3052 Hz. Subjects read aloud consonant-vowel syllables (18-19 consonants followed by /a/, /u/ or /i/), and syllable timing was hand-annotated off-line from synchronized microphone recordings. The audio was removed from the released data.
